comment: Overreacts to small things and handles conflict poorly. Can be condescending and makes the class uncomfortable when things don't go his way. Be careful very little patience or professionalism when challenged.

If you show up to every class its almost impossible to get below an A. The class is not hard and he often gives extra credit for showing up to class. He goes slow and can be a bit repetitive but he makes sure no one is left behind. I took the excel competency exam for the b school after this class having never used excel before and got a 98%.

Very easy class with even a modicum of effort. He gave a significant number of extra credit points and basically all assignments were by the book. He gave us sheets stating exactly what would be on the test beforehand.

My only complaint is that he is extremely inflexible and his extreme politeness borders on passive aggressiveness.

Don't take the excel class very much a waste of time if you are doing it for the compentency exam. He is nice but class is very slow and he has two tests and requires a lot of effort for just a half credit. The school gives practice tests for the bschool exam and that is the only thing you need truly.

I took him for software tools using Excel, a half-credit class. It was super easy, but he is not the best professor and isn't compromising. The class is an absolute breeze if you have sub-par Excel skills. There are extra credit opportunities, which are super easy and should be taken advantage of. Expect to teach yourself, but free A nonetheless.

I would say to only take this class if you have to. By far the worst class I have ever taken. Outdated program with no real application to the real-world, it's all just memorization of his lines of code from class. He seems like a decent guy, but the class is terrible.

Professor Whitaker doesn't really explain anything just gives you scripts that you memorize for the tests. Don't expect an A even if you get a 99% as he curves to only give 2 students an A in his classes. Pretty much a waste of time. You learn outdated material and you also get a poor grade.

Don't expect this class to be easy and get ready in advance before the semester begins. However, Dr. Whitaker is a really great professor and tries his best to help his students to get good grades. You can trust everything he says except "I don't want students to memorize". Just memorize everything by practice typing without looking at anything.

Dr. Whitaker tells you exactly what you need to do in order to succeed in his class. So long as you read the textbook (free through UR), do the homework and pay attention in class you can do well. He also offers up to 5% extra credit which is often harder than regular homework, but makes your better prepared for tests. This also applies to MGMT325.

Prepare to seriously self-teach yourself if you aren't a student who has prior knowledge or a student who can learn simply by watching someone go through the steps once. Class materials are taken off blackboard immediately following class, leaving you with nothing to practice with on your own. Biggest regret within RSB is not dropping this class.

Dr. Whitaker is one of the best professors that the business school has to offer. He really cares about not only how much you learn in the course, but even more about finding your career path and setting you up for the future. His MGMT 325 course is tough, but an A or B is still possible provided you work hard. Would recommend 10/10 times.

Professor Whitaker is truly a great professor. His energy and enthusiasm along with inspirational career advice makes him highly respected by students. Sometimes his interactions with students seem cheesy and forced, but they're not. Whitaker genuinely cares about his students and it's clear his main goal includes keeping students motivated.
NOT helpful outside class for class material. But very helpful on career plan issues. very insightful.

His grading is by rank, the best groups get As... the rest get scraps. If you are underperforming there is no real help or guidance, and you get what you get, even if there are things out of your control. His enthusiasm is welcome in the morning.

Not helpful outside of class. Uses forced grade distribution, so some good students get screwed. If he was a true educator and not driven by ego, the goal should be as many A's as students there are wiling to work for it.

Talks his class up a lot on the first day to weed out the lazy kids.  Don't be scared to take his OM class.  Yeah, you're gunna have to read the textbook, but its only about 10 pages per class.  His tests are easy, but a little challenging to finish.  I would take him if you actually want to learn about OM.

He is a really nice guy and he really cares.  It is a tough class, and you have to work, but, again, he is a great guy, with great experience, who really cares about his students.  Also, a fair grader.
smart, confident, teaching?? questionably, grading--- poor - in part based on his idea of having a forced distribution of grades of each class

Super helpful and accommodating. Really wants you to learn and do well in his class, and will do all he can to ensure that happens. Lots of real world examples, and hands on learning. Overall a great professor!! One of my favorites at UR

This professor is very knowledgeable of the material. He applies class to the real world. Assignments are graded based on his discretion mostly on a scale from 1-12 (confusing but he's very willing to explain your grade).
This class is challenging but not hard. Professor Whitaker is very clear about his expectations and he will bend over backwards to help you. Tries to make the class geared towards the real world.
